text:
alice: Heads up — seeing a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate after last night's runtime + quant kernel swap on prod. baseline was ~78% -> now ~49% for app-tier traffic. Not traffic spike.
ben: can you paste the hit-rate graphs and the exact kernel/quant build IDs?
alice: quick numbers from our dashboard: 
```
model: llama-3b-quant-v2
kernel: runtime-kernel-2026-03-17-v3
quant-profile: q4_0_dynamic
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 78.1% (2026-03-16)
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 49.3% (2026-03-18)
avg_latency.p50: +12ms
```
deploy-bot: deploy: runtime-kernel-2026-03-17-v3 rolled to prod at 1987649800 by ci/cd (canary -> 100%).
carol: hmm — last kernel had an attention optim change that changed how past_kv buffers are packed (added 8-byte alignment and a new serialization header). if the cache key includes raw bytes of past_kv or a binary hash of the serialized prefix, that will break key equality.
dave: +1. We saw similar in staging when we changed the KV layout for fused-attn. Quick test: try legacy keying toggle on one canary instance and replay traffic to see if x-prefix-cache-hit flips back. header we use is `x-prefix-cache-hit: 1/0`.
alice: running canary with LEGACY_KV_KEYING=1 now on 3 instances. replaying 5m sample set.
```
# curl snippet to test single request header
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Prefer: x-prefix-cache-test" \
  -d '{"model":"llama-3b-quant-v2","input":"<prefilled prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood-infer/prod/generate | jq -r '.meta.headers["x-prefix-cache-hit"]'
```
alice: after enabling legacy keying on canary, sample shows x-prefix-cache-hit = 1 for 74% of requests (was 49% on mainline). so the kernel change is almost certainly the culprit.
eva: quant profile might also affect serialized dtype/scale metadata included in keying. if key includes quant params we need canonicalization across profiles, or backwards-compatible key derivation.
ben: what's the rollback plan? do we revert kernel or ship a small compatibility patch?
alice: short-term: rollback kernel to runtime-kernel-2026-03-10-v2 (previous) for full fleet — that will restore hit-rate quickly. medium-term: patch runtime to compute a canonicalized prefix-key that ignores non-functional header bytes (alignment, added version tag) and supports a dual-hash lookup (new_key OR legacy_key) for N days.
dave: I'll own the rollback. starting canary rollback now (3 nodes), measuring hit-rate and latency; will stop and escalate if anything else pops. oncall: @carol please watch memory/eviction if legacy keying increases key cardinality.
deploy-bot: rollback: runtime-kernel-2026-03-10-v2 started at 1987654200 by ops/dave (canary).
deploy-bot: rollback: runtime-kernel-2026-03-10-v2 completed to 100% at 1987654380.
alice: post-rollback metrics: prefix_cache.hit_rate back to 77.4%, p50 latency baseline. looks good.
ben: ok let's create a short postmortem and a patch PR for canonical keying + dual-lookup. include regression test that simulates small changes in serialization.
eva: i'll draft the PR with unit tests for key canonicalization and a migration plan (dual-hash for 7 days).
carol: also add telemetry that logs when we hit legacy_key fallback so we can measure traffic during migration.
dave: closing the incident. assigning follow-ups in the ticket. thanks team. :thumbsup:
